free_tier.stated: 20 MB per file, no subscription: 'Custom emojis, a 20MB file upload limit and a server-specific profile picture with no subscription required.' No published total-storage cap and no paid tier that raises the file size.

egress.terms: Free and — importantly — UNSIGNED. Autumn 301s to cdn.stoatusercontent.com and the object URL is a bare path with no expiry parameters, unlike Discord. So a stored URL stays valid and is trivially Cloudflare-cacheable.

tooling: Genuinely open: 'Our public API is so powerful that we use it ourselves for the official apps', API root answers live (GET https://api.revolt.chat/ -> {"stoat":"0.16.2","revolt":"0.16.2", features...}). Backend is open source (revoltchat/autumn, stoatchat/*). Self-hostable, which is both the appeal and the caveat.
chaining: Unlimited servers x unlimited channels with a 20 MB cap, so 1 TB needs ~52,000 uploads. With no signed URLs, the reads are the easy part; the writes are the bottleneck.
limits_note: 20 MB per file is fixed and low; there is no path to a bigger unit. Upload limits are server-configurable only on SELF-hosted instances ('Upload limits are controlled via the Autumn config'), so on the public instance you are stuck at 20 MB.
reliability_note: Smaller operator, recent rebrand to Stoat, and the public instance runs human-verification step on signup. Data longevity is a real question for a 20 TiB cold archive; treat as experimental.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
